description: 48 original CC0-1.0 hand-authored adversarial text samples (24 subtle clean-lexicon AI-pattern passages + 24 grounded clean passages, balanced ZH/EN) spanning keyword co-occurrence, punctuation micro-habits, narrative sandwich framing, syntactic skeleton echo, statistical monotony, and multi-signal prose. Designed to expose blind spots when v1 single-word rules saturate.

In October we ran SQLite in WAL mode on a single 4-vCPU box to handle webhook deduplication for 1.2 million daily events. Median write latency stayed at 0.6 ms, and disk usage leveled off at 3.4 GB once the 7-day pruning cron stabilized.

The only surprise hit during Sunday vacuum runs, which blocked incoming writers for 11 seconds and triggered 42 client retries. Switching from full `VACUUM` to `PRAGMA incremental_vacuum(2000)` every hour removed the stall completely.

We do not plan to move this service to Postgres until daily volume exceeds 8 million events or we need multi-region active writes.

Every November my uncle tapes bubble wrap along the north glass of his cedar greenhouse. One roll costs fourteen dollars at the hardware store off Route 9 and lasts two winters if the mice stay out of the shed.

Inside, forty Meyer lemon saplings sit on cinder-block benches beside a rusted kerosene heater. When the thermometer drops below 38 degrees Fahrenheit, he walks out in rubber boots at midnight with a headlamp and cracks the wick up a quarter turn.

The lemons never turn sweet enough for eating raw, so my aunt slices them paper-thin with coarse salt and packs six quart jars before Christmas.
